session.title: Switchy 1.0.24: Codex 0.160's websocket relayed instead of refused with 426; Codex cybersecurity flags traced to ~/.codex developer_instructions
session.purpose: Carry out worker_brief_codex_0160_ws.md: codex-cli 0.160.0 logged 'failed to connect to websocket: HTTP error: 426 Upgrade Required' against ws://127.0.0.1:15721/backend-api/codex/responses and interactive Codex was blocked; find where the 426 came from, make the proxy accept and relay the websocket without breaking the HTTP path, verify, archive the brief. the user then pushed for parity with the pre-0.160 behaviour (usage-limit failover, Usage Statistics), asked which quota rotated registered2nd out, had the decision-log entry checked against the criteria, and asked why some GameTrainers Codex sessions stopped working.
outcomes: Root cause: the 426 was Switchy's own, by design since 2026-09-21: GET /backend-api/codex/responses was bound to a refusal handler so Codex would fall back to HTTP. Codex 0.160 keeps one websocket across turns (later turns are increments via previous_response_id), treats only a handshake 426 as 'use HTTP' (sticky for the session) and logs it as an ERROR. Nothing came from chatgpt.com.

Fix (src-tauri/src/proxy/codex_ws.rs; .with_upgrades() in proxy/server.rs; HTTP/1.1 client in proxy/http_client.rs): the websocket is relayed frame by frame to chatgpt.com with the account the router picks at connect (exit check, that account's login). An account refusing the handshake, or refusing a turn for usage before any of it reached Codex, is passed over and the turn is resent on the next account with its opening events held back; when the pool's choice changes or the account was refused, the connection closes between turns and Codex reconnects on the new account. 426 remains only when the first choice is not a ChatGPT login or no account accepts the handshake. No frame size limit: a live 38 MB turn had been cut by tungstenite's 16 MB default.

Usage Statistics: finished websocket turns are logged as streamed requests with tokens on the serving account, refusals as errors against the refusing account; Codex's generate:false warm-up is not counted. Codex 0.160 renamed its session header to session-id; proxy/session.rs now reads it, so Codex sessions are no longer split per request (HTTP path too).

Verified on installed 1.0.24 (commits 5829b07d, 26c6e8ac, 4bb8edec, bfd11f38): codex exec logs 'successfully connected to websocket: ws://127.0.0.1:15721/backend-api/codex/responses' with no 426 and answers ok; a turn driven through codex app-server completes; a direct POST to the HTTP path still streams response.completed; websocket turns at 22:17 and 22:18 logged with 27,112 input / 5 output / 12,544 cached tokens; an HTTP row at 22:27 carries Codex's real session id. 478 proxy tests pass. Not verified live: the usage-limit failover (no account at 100%), the 38 MB session reconnecting, a websocket row's session id.

Not released: 1.0.24 is committed on local main (4 commits ahead of origin), installers/Switchy_1.0.24_x64-setup.exe and .msi built and installed on this machine; no push, no macOS DMG, no public release.

Answer given: the last automatic switch off registered2nd@gmail.com was Codex at 21:27:39 on 2026-10-04 (rotation, 'Near its usage limit') when its weekly (7-day) window reached 99% (threshold 99%), resetting 2026-10-09 21:00; its Claude account last rotated out at 15:12:52 the same day.
Decision-log entry trimmed to the cross-cutting choice after checking recordkeeping_model.md § Decision: warm-up exclusion, frame size limit and usage-log details are local to codex_ws.rs.

Codex 'This content was flagged for possible cybersecurity risk' failures (GameTrainers sessions from 2026-10-04 16:59 on; 0 of 4 sessions flagged on 10-03) were not Switchy or Orca: replaying a flagged session's opening context through the proxy one piece at a time showed every flagged combination contained the developer_instructions block 'Codex operates in local execution mode…' from Windows ~/.codex/config.toml (set 2026-09-28 as a test, line 8 comment); dropping only it passed. It also flagged with Switchy bypassed (direct to chatgpt.com, 3/3). Removed lines 9-190 at the user's direction (backup ~/.codex/config.toml.before_devinstr_removal_2026-10-05); 4/4 codex exec runs from C:/Projects/GameTrainers then answered ok. gpt-lean.md was not restored because it opens with the same text. WSL ~/.codex/config.toml has no such block. Open GameTrainers sessions must be started fresh; a resumed one replays the flagged text.
Noted, not acted on: codex_engine retries session files left by dead Codex windows forever (log lines 'could not connect … actively refused' every few seconds); out of the brief's scope.

My mistake this session: opened a visible PowerShell window on the user's desktop through windows-mcp to run interactive codex; he objected; it was closed and the check redone headlessly through codex app-server.
session.latest_summary: 1.0.24 (local, unreleased) relays Codex 0.160's websocket with per-connection accounts, usage-limit failover and usage logging; the GameTrainers cybersecurity flags came from a developer_instructions block in ~/.codex/config.toml, now removed.
